title: The Weight of Choice
text:
Every professional decision carries an ethical dimension, even when it appears purely technical. Engineers who approve a design, or doctors who prescribe a treatment, are accountable for the consequences that follow, whether or not those consequences were foreseen. Responsibility, in this sense, cannot be delegated entirely to a procedure or a manual.

Yet accountability is often diffused across large organisations, where many people contribute small pieces of a single outcome. This diffusion can make wrongdoing seem nobody's fault in particular. For this reason, many ethicists argue that institutions should design clear lines of responsibility, so that every decision can be traced back to someone who must answer for it.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, who is accountable for the consequences of a decision?
options: The engineers and doctors who make the decision
The manuals that guide the procedure
The organisation as an abstract entity
Nobody, because consequences cannot be predicted

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why can wrongdoing seem to be nobody's fault?
options: Responsibility is diffused across many people in large organisations
Small contributions always cause the most damage

questions.text: What does the author imply about relying on procedures to avoid moral responsibility?
options: It is not sufficient, because responsibility cannot be fully handed over to a procedure
It is the best way to ensure that no one is blamed
It removes the need for professional judgement
It is required by law in every profession

questions.text: What can be inferred about the purpose of clear lines of responsibility?
options: They aim to make it possible to hold a specific person answerable for each decision
They are intended to remove all ethical debate from institutions
They are meant to spread blame evenly across every employee
They replace the need for individual professional ethics

paragraph_translations: Toda decisão profissional carrega uma dimensão ética, mesmo quando parece puramente técnica. Engenheiros que aprovam um projeto, ou médicos que prescrevem um tratamento, são responsáveis pelas consequências que se seguem, quer elas tenham sido previstas ou não. A responsabilidade, nesse sentido, não pode ser totalmente delegada a um procedimento ou a um manual.

Ainda assim, a responsabilidade costuma ser difundida em grandes organizações, onde muitas pessoas contribuem com pequenas partes de um mesmo resultado. Essa difusão pode fazer com que a falha pareça não ser culpa de ninguém em particular. Por isso, muitos eticistas defendem que as instituições devem definir linhas claras de responsabilidade, para que cada decisão possa ser atribuída a alguém que deva prestar contas por ela.
